summary: The pooled platform signup bootstrap can now disable a sign-in provider it manages, as long as at least one provider stays enabled.
userImpact: Operators can withdraw a platform sign-in method (for example Apple) by setting it to disabled in the startup identity-provider bundle; it then no longer appears on the cloud signup page.
configuration: An identity provider in the pooled startup bundle may set enabled to false. A bundle in which every provider is disabled is still rejected before any import authority is granted.
security: The bootstrap capability is unchanged in kind: it still covers only the bundle's listed platform providers, rejects LDAP, non-direct authentication and verified email linking, and is revoked after the receipt is written.
documentation: The configuration reference describes the pooled-mode bootstrap limits, including disabling a managed provider.
rollback: Re-enable the provider in the bundle, or roll back to the previous host release; a disabled provider row is re-enabled by the next bundle that marks it enabled.
validation: The configuration bootstrap suite covers a bundle that disables one provider while keeping another enabled, and rejects a bundle whose only provider is disabled.

customerDocumentation.reason: Only operators who mount a pooled startup signup bundle are affected, and the configuration reference covers it.
